title: Made a horror game prototype in one shot from a detailed GDD, then tuned it
author: Aggressive-Actuary36
selftext:
This is **DEAD AIR**, a horror game parody of the movie **Late Night with the Devil**, with low-poly animal characters.

You are a late night TV host in 1986. You interview strange guests and try to get more viewers. When guests become more unstable, ratings go up. But if you push too much, something bad happens on live TV.

I made the first playable prototype in one shot with AI, using a detailed GDD. After that, I kept tuning the game on the same base.

The important part for me was preparing the GDD before implementation.

The document covered the game loop, rules, how a run progresses, and how the game should look and feel. Not just “make a horror card game.” It needed to explain how all these parts work together.

Then I gave this GDD to the coding agent to build the initial prototype.

The first result was already quite complete for a prototype. Gameplay and presentation were working together, so I could play it and judge the whole experience. It was not just separate systems waiting to be connected.

After that, I played it, found what felt wrong, adjusted it, and played again. Having the whole game working early made it easier to decide what needed tuning.

**“One shot” means the initial prototype, not the final game with no changes.**

For me, this was more interesting than generating code or assets separately. Make the design clear first, get a solid playable version in one pass, then improve it through actual play.

Curious how much detail other people put in their GDD before giving it to a coding agent.
